# Researching and ingesting wiki evidence

Choose the mode explicitly from the request. An unspecified request to use this
role is not permission to process the whole backlog; clarify the intended task.
Treat `` as the request when the host has not substituted it.

- **Discover sources on a topic:** read [discovery](references/discover.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md),
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md), and
  [efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md). Research perspectives
  return candidates without writing. Use the capture route only within the
  requested scope; a request for candidates alone remains read-only.
- **Capture named URLs or saved web pages:** read [named capture](references/capture.md)
  and [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md). Skip broad topic research;
  preserve deduplication, declines and capture checks.
- **Capture a named format or service:** read its complete route:
  [PDF](references/clip-pdf.md), [Word](references/clip-docx.md),
  [PowerPoint](references/clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheets](references/clip-xlsx.md),
  [GitHub repository](references/clip-gh.md), or
  [Confluence](references/clip-confluence.md). These routes include prerequisite
  checks; missing converters or authentication never justify fabricated evidence.
- **Ingest named existing clippings:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), and
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md). Use the exact source set;
  do not rediscover it or silently expand to the global backlog.
- **Process new or un-ingested clippings without a filename:** read
  [ingestion](references/ingest.md) and the
  [hash-join backlog contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md).
  Determine eligibility before writing. Preserve already summarized sources and
  reject restricted evidence as support. If nothing eligible is pending, report
  that without opening an operation, logging, committing or refreshing indexes.

Capture-only requests create evidence, never derived source or concept pages.
Ingestion needs authorization for that source set; an explicitly requested full
research-and-ingest flow already provides it. Only capture tools write raw
artifacts, and agents never edit their bodies. Read
[evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) before assessing fidelity,
quoting or synthesizing; preserve restrictions and platform-specific sections.

Before the first authorized mutation, read
[operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md). Finish the
scoped validation, log, commit, sync and remote verification unless publication
is held. Reuse an enclosing operation when it owns the work; preserve other
writers' edits. For concept reuse and relationship changes read
[efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md).
Mode is the named-format capture for spreadsheets. I'll read the spreadsheet route only; the operations reference isn't needed because I'm not mutating anything.

5	# Clipping a spreadsheet into the wiki
6	
7	The HTML clipper (`clip.mjs` → Defuddle) handles **HTML** pages only,
8	`clip-pdf` handles **PDFs**, and `clip-docx` handles **Word** documents. A
9	workbook — sheets of cells, where meaning lives in which value sits against
10	which label — falls to none of those. This reference covers the spreadsheet path.
11	**The canonical stored artifact is the extracted Markdown, never the binary
12	workbook** — that keeps the vault greppable, diffable and answerable, and makes
13	`[[note]]` provenance resolve to a real Markdown clipping rather than to an
14	opaque attachment.
15	
16	**Never reach a workbook by converting it to PDF and running `clip-pdf`.** That
17	is the exact case `clip-pdf` warns about: row/label pairings get rebuilt from
18	horizontal position, and a flattened table reads clean while pairing the wrong
19	number with the wrong label. A spreadsheet is the worst document to put through
20	it, because the pairing *is* the content.
21	
22	## How it works
23	
24	`clip-xlsx.mjs` converts with **LibreOffice** (`soffice --headless --convert-to
25	html`, which renders every sheet as a table), then pipes that HTML through
26	**pandoc** to Markdown with `--wrap=none`, and writes `raw/clippings/<slug>.md`
27	with the standard clipping frontmatter (`source`, `created`, `tags:[clippings]`,
28	`quality`, `source-hash`). The title is derived from the filename — a workbook
29	carries no title worth trusting.
30	
31	- **`soffice` is invoked by bare name on purpose**, so PATHEXT selects the
32	  console shim (`soffice.com`); `soffice.exe` is the GUI build and writes nothing
33	  to stdout. Both converters run through Node's `execFileSync` — do **not** shell
34	  out to them from a Bash tool.
35	- **Two failures that look alike are handled differently.** A missing LibreOffice
36	  is fatal and stops the run with an install pointer: fix the install. A workbook
37	  that *itself* fails to convert (corrupt or password-protected) returns `failed`
38	  so a batch run continues. Report it for manual handling; never invent the cells.
39	- **Duplicates are caught by content hash**, not just by path, so a renamed or
40	  moved workbook whose contents the vault already holds is recognized rather than
41	  clipped twice under a second slug.
42	
43	## Steps
44	
45	1. **Preflight** (once): confirm both converters are installed — `soffice
46	   --version` and `pandoc -v`. If LibreOffice is missing, tell the user to
47	   install it (https://www.libreoffice.org/download/) and stop; do not fabricate
48	   cell values or retype the workbook by hand.
49	2. **Clip** (this is the only writer to `raw/` for workbooks):
50	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-xlsx.mjs" "<path/to/file.xlsx>" --source="<canonical-url-if-any>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>"`
51	   - `--source` is the citable origin. Omit it for a purely local file and the
52	     file path is recorded as the source; never invent a URL to fill the field.
53	   - **`--topic` whenever this clip belongs to a research run** — pass the topic
54	     string researcher discovery was given, identical across every clip in the run,
55	     so maintainer triage can group the run's leftovers together. **Topic is recorded
56	     going forward only and no tool can retro-fit it**, so a clip made without it
57	     is an *Unattributed* triage row permanently. Omit it only when there is no
58	     research run behind the clip; never invent one.
59	   - `--quality` is your credibility judgment of the workbook as a source, which
60	     is separate from how cleanly it extracted.
61	3. **Verify** the clipping landed: read `raw/clippings/<slug>.md` and confirm the
62	   sheets came through as real tables with their labels still attached to their
63	   values. Conversion is lossy on formulas, merged cells, charts and multi-row
64	   headers — it captures rendered values, not the model behind them.
65	   - A `thin` result (under 100 words) records a decline so it is not retried
66	     blindly. **Unlike `clip-docx`, this clipper has no `--allow-short`
67	     override** — a genuinely tiny but complete workbook needs the decline
68	     cleared or the content captured another way. Say so rather than pretending
69	     the clip succeeded.
70	4. **Only when ingestion is authorized, follow [ingestion](ingest.md)** for this exact clipping — summarize
71	   into `wiki/sources/`, cross-reference, index, log. Ingestion requires
72	   authorization for this scope; reuse explicit session authorization.
73	
74	## Guardrails
75	
76	- **Never edit the body of anything under `raw/`** — clipped text is immutable
77	  source-of-truth (guardrail #1). Frontmatter is pipeline state, tooling-only.
78	- `clip-xlsx.mjs` is the **sole writer** to `raw/` for workbooks — the model never
79	  writes the clipping by hand (that would bypass dedup, decline and hashing, and
80	  the ingest backlog joins on exactly that hash).
81	- **Fidelity, not truth**: a faithful extraction of the wrong workbook is still
82	  wrong, and a converted sheet can silently lose the structure that gave a number
83	  its meaning — verify any figure against the workbook before it lands on a wiki
84	  page (guardrail #5).
85	
86	## Completion
87	
88	For a standalone clip, open an operation before the clipping helper writes, verify
89	its returned paths and extraction diagnostics, log once, commit, push and verify
90	remote publication through the shared operations contract. During discovery,
91	use the enclosing operation and report the results to its owner for completion.
92	Pass `--since <saved-token>` to the clipping helper so every written path enters
93	that operation's ledger. Capture-only requests end after this completion and
94	create no derived source or concept pages.
95	Capturing evidence does not by itself authorize ingestion; reuse explicit
96	discover-and-ingest authorization when it is already present.

# Clipping a spreadsheet into the wiki

The HTML clipper (`clip.mjs` → Defuddle) handles **HTML** pages only,
`clip-pdf` handles **PDFs**, and `clip-docx` handles **Word** documents. A
workbook — sheets of cells, where meaning lives in which value sits against
which label — falls to none of those. This reference covers the spreadsheet path.
**The canonical stored artifact is the extracted Markdown, never the binary
workbook** — that keeps the vault greppable, diffable and answerable, and makes
`[[note]]` provenance resolve to a real Markdown clipping rather than to an
opaque attachment.

**Never reach a workbook by converting it to PDF and running `clip-pdf`.** That
is the exact case `clip-pdf` warns about: row/label pairings get rebuilt from
horizontal position, and a flattened table reads clean while pairing the wrong
number with the wrong label. A spreadsheet is the worst document to put through
it, because the pairing *is* the content.

## How it works

`clip-xlsx.mjs` converts with **LibreOffice** (`soffice --headless --convert-to
html`, which renders every sheet as a table), then pipes that HTML through
**pandoc** to Markdown with `--wrap=none`, and writes `raw/clippings/<slug>.md`
with the standard clipping frontmatter (`source`, `created`, `tags:[clippings]`,
`quality`, `source-hash`). The title is derived from the filename — a workbook
carries no title worth trusting.

- **`soffice` is invoked by bare name on purpose**, so PATHEXT selects the
  console shim (`soffice.com`); `soffice.exe` is the GUI build and writes nothing
  to stdout. Both converters run through Node's `execFileSync` — do **not** shell
  out to them from a Bash tool.
- **Two failures that look alike are handled differently.** A missing LibreOffice
  is fatal and stops the run with an install pointer: fix the install. A workbook
  that *itself* fails to convert (corrupt or password-protected) returns `failed`
  so a batch run continues. Report it for manual handling; never invent the cells.
- **Duplicates are caught by content hash**, not just by path, so a renamed or
  moved workbook whose contents the vault already holds is recognized rather than
  clipped twice under a second slug.

## Steps

1. **Preflight** (once): confirm both converters are installed — `soffice
   --version` and `pandoc -v`. If LibreOffice is missing, tell the user to
   install it (https://www.libreoffice.org/download/) and stop; do not fabricate
   cell values or retype the workbook by hand.
2. **Clip** (this is the only writer to `raw/` for workbooks):
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-xlsx.mjs" "<path/to/file.xlsx>" --source="<canonical-url-if-any>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>"`
   - `--source` is the citable origin. Omit it for a purely local file and the
     file path is recorded as the source; never invent a URL to fill the field.
   - **`--topic` whenever this clip belongs to a research run** — pass the topic
     string researcher discovery was given, identical across every clip in the run,
     so maintainer triage can group the run's leftovers together. **Topic is recorded
     going forward only and no tool can retro-fit it**, so a clip made without it
     is an *Unattributed* triage row permanently. Omit it only when there is no
     research run behind the clip; never invent one.
   - `--quality` is your credibility judgment of the workbook as a source, which
     is separate from how cleanly it extracted.
3. **Verify** the clipping landed: read `raw/clippings/<slug>.md` and confirm the
   sheets came through as real tables with their labels still attached to their
   values. Conversion is lossy on formulas, merged cells, charts and multi-row
   headers — it captures rendered values, not the model behind them.
   - A `thin` result (under 100 words) records a decline so it is not retried
     blindly. **Unlike `clip-docx`, this clipper has no `--allow-short`
     override** — a genuinely tiny but complete workbook needs the decline
     cleared or the content captured another way. Say so rather than pretending
     the clip succeeded.
4. **Only when ingestion is authorized, follow [ingestion](ingest.md)** for this exact clipping — summarize
   into `wiki/sources/`, cross-reference, index, log. Ingestion requires
   authorization for this scope; reuse explicit session authorization.

## Guardrails

- **Never edit the body of anything under `raw/`** — clipped text is immutable
  source-of-truth (guardrail #1). Frontmatter is pipeline state, tooling-only.
- `clip-xlsx.mjs` is the **sole writer** to `raw/` for workbooks — the model never
  writes the clipping by hand (that would bypass dedup, decline and hashing, and
  the ingest backlog joins on exactly that hash).
- **Fidelity, not truth**: a faithful extraction of the wrong workbook is still
  wrong, and a converted sheet can silently lose the structure that gave a number
  its meaning — verify any figure against the workbook before it lands on a wiki
  page (guardrail #5).

## Completion

For a standalone clip, open an operation before the clipping helper writes, verify
its returned paths and extraction diagnostics, log once, commit, push and verify
remote publication through the shared operations contract. During discovery,
use the enclosing operation and report the results to its owner for completion.
Pass `--since <saved-token>` to the clipping helper so every written path enters
that operation's ledger. Capture-only requests end after this completion and
create no derived source or concept pages.
Capturing evidence does not by itself authorize ingestion; reuse explicit
discover-and-ingest authorization when it is already present.

**Chosen skill:** `wiki-master:wiki-researcher`, invoked through the Skill tool.

**Role and mode:** Researcher, in the "capture a named format or service" mode, using the spreadsheet route. The request names one file (`report.xlsx`) and asks for it as evidence. That rules out topic discovery, ingestion and backlog processing.

**Loaded references:** Only `skills/wiki-researcher/references/clip-xlsx.md`. It points to the access and operations references, but those are for execution, so I didn't open them. I also didn't open the evidence reference, which is only needed before quoting figures.

**What the workflow would do (not executed):**
- Check that `soffice --version` and `pandoc -v` both work. If LibreOffice is missing, stop and point the user to the install page. Never retype cells by hand.
- Open an operation, then run `clip-xlsx.mjs` on the file. Use `--source` only if there's a real canonical URL, and `--topic` only if this belongs to a research run.
- Check that `raw/clippings/<slug>.md` has real tables with labels still attached to their values.
- Log, commit, push and verify the remote.

**Boundaries and caveats:**
- **Capture only:** The result is a raw clipping. It creates no `wiki/sources/` or concept pages, and ingestion would need separate authorization.
- **Not PDF:** The workbook must never be converted to PDF and run through `clip-pdf`, because that can pair the wrong number with the wrong label.
- **Raw clippings are immutable:** Only the clipper writes to `raw/`, and nobody edits clipping bodies.
- **Short workbooks:** A clip under 100 words is declined as `thin`, and this clipper has no `--allow-short` override.
- **Lossy conversion:** Formulas, merged cells, charts and multi-row headers can be lost, so figures need checking against the workbook.
- **Publication approval:** The commit, push and remote verification happen only if publication isn't held. The user would need to confirm that.
- **Missing details:** I need the actual path of `report.xlsx` and whether it belongs to a research topic. The probe says it was "provided", but no path was given.

I ran no commands, made no captures and didn't touch any vault.
